$comment: Forged Light 2, revised 2026-11-13 to the developer-tool look and, the same day, to a lifted, tinted palette (ADR-136, second revision; values re-derived 2026-11-14 from the brief by lightness only, deviations listed in the ADR). The single source of the design tokens: `cargo xtask design-tokens` writes tokens.css into every surface and `--check` fails CI when a copy drifts. Keys under each group are custom-property names without the leading `--`; nested groups join with `-` (type.type-body.size -> --type-body-size). Keys starting with `$` are comments. A new colour role is a change here with a contrast pair below, never a literal in a surface's stylesheet (`cargo xtask design-tokens --literals <dir>` finds them).

theme.$comment: One meaning per colour: teal = trust, secure, the primary action; bronze = value, coins, proof, warmth; green = verified or confirmed; amber = needs a look, testnet, paused; coral = error or irreversible; blue = information or research; steel = reference. Dark is the brand's home theme and the default when the OS states no preference; its ground is a deep teal-navy, not a hue-free black, and a card lifts 1.25:1 off it so it reads as lit rather than switched off. Light is warm paper, not a grey inversion. surface-1 is a card and the fill of every input and secondary button; surface-2 a hover row; surface-3 a pressed one; a selected row is accent-subtle over surface-1 (a teal tint, not a darker beige). Tiers per meaning: the plain role (accent-text, bronze, success, warn, danger, info, steel) is safe as body text on every surface and on its own chip; *-subtle is the chip ground (tint + 1 px role edge + role ink + icon and word); *-fill is solid, for dots, alert edges and counters under on-fill ink only, never a chip ground; bronze-display is bronze for figures of 24 px and up (3:1). Bronze is one ramp per theme (role, text, display, fill, forge stops and chart-2 are its steps or var() references to them), and the hue-families gate holds each meaning to one hue. border-control is the edge of an input or checkbox (3:1, SC 1.4.11); border and border-strong are hairlines. deco-* are translucent large fills for grad-hero and backdrops and are never text or meaning; the hero's text is gated on deco-teal over surface-1, and text-3 is never set on the hero. Chart and gradient tokens live here, not in global, because a var() resolves where it is declared: a nested data-theme must re-declare them.

dark.grad-hero: radial-gradient(70% 60% at 50% 0%, var(--deco-teal) 0%, transparent 70%), linear-gradient(180deg, var(--surface-1) 0%, var(--bg) 100%)

light.grad-hero: radial-gradient(70% 60% at 50% 0%, var(--deco-teal) 0%, transparent 70%), linear-gradient(180deg, var(--surface-1) 0%, var(--bg) 100%)

font.$comment: Inter for everything (variable, self-hosted, opsz axis); JetBrains Mono for code, addresses, hashes and figures. Manrope is retired.
font.font-mono: "JetBrains Mono Variable", "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, Consolas, monospace

type.$comment: One scale for every surface: 12/13/14/16/20/24/32/40/56. Weights 400/500/600 only. Body 1.5, headings 1.2; display sizes track -0.02em. `size-phone` is the phone step, taken from the same scale.

space.$comment: 4 px base; the step number is px / 4.

radius.$comment: Nothing above 12 px. The pill is for status dots and chips only, never a button or card.

elevation.$comment: flat = surface + border (every card); raised = shadow-md + shadow-inset on hover and selected; floating = glass + shadow-lg (header and the command palette only).

motion.$comment: Short, linear-feeling, no spring or overshoot.

chart.$comment: The series colours are per theme (theme.*.chart-1 to chart-6, in the same order in both: teal, bronze, blue, neutral, chart-5 (dark #c58cff, light #7c3aed; its hue is an open decision for Eric, forged-light-2.md §8), copper). Status colours and fills are never series colours; chart-3 shares the blue family with info by exception, because a series never appears as a chip and info always carries its icon and word. Charts sit on bg, surface-1 or surface-2, never on a pressed or selected surface-3. Fills are the stroke at chart-fill-alpha.

reduced-motion.$comment: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce zeroes every duration; end states still apply.

chart-distinctness.$comment: Worst OKLab distance between any two series, under normal vision and simulated deuteranopia and protanopia (Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes 2009, severity 1.0, applied in linear sRGB). Below min-distance two series read as one at chart sizes; the xtask test fails. An ink series is one near the text colour (OKLab L above ink-lightness.dark on the dark ground, below ink-lightness.light on paper); more than max-ink-series of them reads as dark smudges on paper or white bars on navy, even when the distance gate passes. The thresholds are design rules, not a standard.

role-distinctness.$comment: One meaning per colour only holds if two meanings never share a colour. Every two roles in a set must be at least min-distance apart in OKLab under normal vision (a set written as an object carries its own min-distance). The text tier is two sets that both hold accent, steel, success, danger and info, one with bronze and one with warn: at 4.5:1 on paper a body-size amber and a body-size bronze cannot be 0.10 apart without moving bronze off its hue, so warn is never shown as bare text; it is always a chip or alert with its icon, word and warn-subtle ground. Steel is a neutral that must still be told from text-2 and text-3, at a smaller distance. Under colour-blind vision the status roles may collapse, which is why every status chip carries its icon and word; value (bronze) and needs-a-look (warn) have no such rule between them, so their solid fills, the tier seen as colour, are cvd-pairs and must stay apart under deuteranopia and protanopia. The thresholds are design rules, not a standard.

hue-families.$comment: Each meaning keeps one hue across its tiers and both themes: the OKLCh hue spread of a family may not exceed max-spread degrees. A failing value is fixed by lightness, not by moving its hue (ADR-136, second revision). The brief's own values span up to 19.5 degrees (warn, dark #ffd43b to light #855600).

contrast-pairs.$comment: [foreground, background, use] or [foreground, background, use, theme]: every pair a component renders, checked in both themes (or the named one) by the generator (WCAG 2.x). A background written `a over b` is the translucent role a composited over the opaque role b, the way a browser paints it: a selected row (accent-subtle over surface-1), the hero's brightest point (deco-teal over surface-1) and each chip ground. use is text (4.5:1), large-text (3:1, 24 px and up) or non-text (3:1), or separation (1.25:1, a house rule, not WCAG: in dark a card and surface-3 against the ground, in light surface-3 against a white card, so a panel reads without a hairline). A role whose value is var(--x) is measured as x. The generator refuses the file when a pair from its required matrix is missing.
